glosses: marks the partner in a mutual action
patterns.usage_note: と names a genuine co-participant: both sides are involved in the same event, which is why it is the particle for 話す, 相談する, 結婚する, けんかする, 付き合う and other reciprocal verbs (似ている takes と only when the resemblance is stated as mutual: 二人はよく似ている; one-way resemblance takes に: 父に似ている). Against sibling 2933 に, which points one way at a recipient or target, と implies the other person is engaged too — 先生に相談する asks for advice, 先生と相談する works the problem out together. With inherently two-sided verbs like 結婚する or けんかする, と cannot be swapped for に at all (×同僚に結婚する).

examples.ruby: 昼休[ひるやす]みに、隣[となり]のクラスの子[こ]と将棋[しょうぎ]で勝負[しょうぶ]した。
examples.english: At lunch break I took on the kid from the next class at shogi.

examples.ruby: 来月[らいげつ]、妹[いもうと]は同僚[どうりょう]と結婚[けっこん]することになった。
examples.english: Next month my little sister is marrying a coworker.

examples.ruby: 家族[かぞく]とじっくり相談[そうだん]してから決[き]めます。
examples.english: I'll make up my mind after talking it through properly with my family.

glosses: marks the person addressed or acted upon
to … at least; as for telling …
patterns.usage_note: The underlying に points one way at the other party: the person told, asked, handed something, or complained to (言う, 頼む, 打ち明ける, 渡す, 叱られる). にゃ is a casual spoken squeeze of には, so it carries the contrastive force of は on top — "him, at any rate" — and it belongs to rough, familiar speech; it would be out of place in writing or with a superior. Compare sibling 0593 と, which makes the other person a partner in the act rather than its target, and sibling 2932, where the same にゃ carries an attitude aimed at someone (子供にゃ優しい) instead of an act of telling or giving.

examples.ruby: こんな話[はなし]、親[おや]にゃとても言[い]えないよ。
examples.english: There's no way on earth I could tell my folks something like this.

examples.ruby: 結果[けっか]は監督[かんとく]にゃ俺[おれ]から伝[つた]えておくよ。
examples.english: I'll be the one to tell the coach the result, at any rate.

examples.ruby: あいつにゃ何[なに]を頼[たの]んでも無駄[むだ]だと思[おも]う。
examples.english: Asking that guy for anything is a waste of breath, if you ask me.
